question.text: For foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) trading in Indian derivative markets, how are their gains typically taxed?

answer.text: Derivative gains are treated as business income taxable at applicable rates regardless of the FPI's structure
FPIs are completely exempt from tax on all derivative transactions in India
FPIs pay a flat 30% tax on all derivative gains regardless of the amount
Gains or losses from derivative transactions on a recognized stock exchange are taxable under capital gains, generally as short-term capital gains or losses

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbooks state that FPI gains or losses from derivative transactions on a recognized stock exchange are taxable under the head capital gains, generally as short-term capital gains or losses. The Trap: FPI derivative income is taxed as capital gains (not business income), and FPIs are not blanket-exempt from tax on Indian derivatives. Note: The capital-gains treatment for FPI derivative transactions is the source-supported position; treaty positions depend on the specific DTAA and are not covered here.
